## Chapter Summary

A relational database stores each fact once and links its tables through keys, so most accounting questions require joining tables. An inner join returns the pairs of rows whose keys match. Columns are qualified with their table or alias, which is required when a name appears in both tables. Because the Charles River database declares no foreign keys, every join is tested by comparing the number of rows it returns with the number it should return. A join to a source document names both the document type and its ID, because each document table numbers its own rows.

A left join keeps every row of the first table, with NULLs where the second table has no match. It lists a whole population, and, written as an anti-join, it finds the records that have no match at all. NOT EXISTS asks the same question, while NOT IN fails silently when its list contains a NULL. A condition on the second table that a NULL cannot meet belongs in the ON clause, because in WHERE it turns the left join into an inner join.

Aggregate functions calculate one value from many rows, and all but `COUNT(*)` skip NULLs. GROUP BY calculates them once per group, and every column of the SELECT list must be grouped or aggregated, even though SQLite does not insist. Grouping by the key rather than the name keeps records that share a name apart. HAVING filters groups after aggregation, while WHERE filters rows before it. A data profile, a few aggregate queries run before a table is used, applies Chapter 2's quality tests in SQL: counts of rows and values, unique keys, the values of code columns, and the dates covered. A join from a header to its lines repeats the header's amounts on every line, so each amount is summed at the level of the table it belongs to.

Subqueries answer questions in two steps. A scalar subquery supplies one value, in the SELECT list or in a condition. A subquery after IN supplies a list, and a correlated subquery runs again for each row of the outer query. In FROM, a subquery forms a derived table, which is summarized first and joined afterward. A query is evaluated, logically, in the order FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY, and LIMIT, which explains where each kind of condition belongs.

Applied to the controller's questions, the queries tied the manufacturing variance of fiscal 2026 to the ledger to the cent. Furniture carries most of it, and it rose in Furniture and Lighting from year to year. The same joins rebuilt the pre-closing trial balance of fiscal 2026 and followed the conversion cost through account 1090 Manufacturing Cost Clearing, where the payroll charged to production rose while the standard cost released by completions stayed nearly flat. Output was nearly flat, so volume explains little of the change. Direct labor stayed within the standard hours, while indirect time grew by about two-thirds and overtime more than doubled. Indirect labor is overhead, so the growth of the variance appears mostly in its overhead part.
